announcer_mentions#ann_caption_source_un.description: No verified public closed-caption or transcript feed exists for MLB broadcasts; MLB.TV and RSN streams are DRM-protected and ToS-restricted, so mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour and mlb.mention_text have no confirmed corpus other than own audio capture plus ASR.
announcer_mentions#ann_caption_source_un.what_would_resolve: A tested legal capture path (OTA/cable caption stream or licensed transcript vendor) that returns timestamped text for >=40 games per crew.

announcer_mentions#ann_crew_visibility.description: Whether the announce crew for each game is published before first pitch in a structured form (schedules often list network only) is unverified; crew substitutions can occur late.
announcer_mentions#ann_crew_visibility.what_would_resolve: Check network press releases and TV listings for a season to see how often the crew is knowable pregame.

announcer_mentions#ann_no_series.description: The series ledger has no MLB announcer-mention series and no rules were sampled, so feed, speakers, counting rules, delay handling and source are unknown and the mechanism is built by analogy to word-count processes rather than from any MLB contract.
announcer_mentions#ann_no_series.what_would_resolve: Locate live MLB mention series or request Kalshi rules; revise after reading verbatim rules.

announcer_mentions#ann_transcript_data.description: No public per-crew transcript corpus for MLB broadcasts is known, and legally capturing audio or captions for large-scale ASR is restricted by broadcast rights; rates would have to be bootstrapped from small own samples.
announcer_mentions#ann_transcript_data.what_would_resolve: Obtain licensed caption archives or build a limited-scope capture for the target crews and verify rights.

extras_and_delay#ext_delay_record.description: Completeness of recorded delay data in the MLB Stats API and box scores for short stoppages is unverified, so historical delay frequencies may be understated.
extras_and_delay#ext_delay_record.what_would_resolve: Compare recorded delays with weather observations for a season at several parks.

extras_and_delay#ext_delay_scope.description: KXMLBDELAY counts any weather delay including start delay and stoppage after the start, but the sampled text does not say how a postponement (no game that day), a suspended-and-resumed game or a very short stoppage is treated.
extras_and_delay#ext_delay_scope.what_would_resolve: Fetch full rules and examples of settled postponed and short-delay games.

extras_and_delay#ext_filing.description: Both series are now filed here but were sampled once each (one postseason extras game, one October delay market); whether regular-season extras markets exist with identical wording and how a doubleheader or a postponed-then-rescheduled game maps to 'originally scheduled' is unseen.
extras_and_delay#ext_filing.what_would_resolve: Sample regular-season KXMLBEXTRAS and KXMLBDELAY rules including a postponed game.

extras_and_delay#ext_lineup_vintage.description: The extras run model needs confirmed starters and lineups, but no input defines the as-of timestamp of the announced card or probable-pitcher changes; roof decisions and postponement calls are likewise timestamped news events.
extras_and_delay#ext_lineup_vintage.what_would_resolve: Own capture of probable pitchers, lineup cards and roof announcements with timestamps for at least one season.

extras_and_delay#ext_stadium_weather.description: Stadium-level high-resolution nowcast and radar integration for each park would be needed to time rain, but only free forecast APIs are available; licensed radar feeds exist but are not obtainable here.
extras_and_delay#ext_stadium_weather.what_would_resolve: Evaluate a paid nowcast vendor or MRMS radar archives against the public forecasts on recorded delays.

first5_markets#f5_filing.description: All five series are now filed here, but each was sampled for one postseason game only; whether regular-season F5 markets carry the same two-day postponement window, and whether the F7 market treats a game ended after the seventh but before nine innings differently, is unseen.
first5_markets#f5_filing.what_would_resolve: Sample regular-season KXMLBF5/F3/F7 rules and a rain-shortened game's settlement.

first5_markets#f5_probable_vintage.description: Probable-pitcher announcements and changes are exposed by MLB feeds but their historical vintage is not archived, which prevents calibrating starter-change risk without own capture. The starter-change risk model therefore cannot be calibrated on five seasons of announced-versus-actual starters from free sources; the Beat-report capture named in required_data has no defined feed.
first5_markets#f5_probable_vintage.what_would_resolve: Capture announcements throughout a season or buy a feed with timestamps.

first5_markets#f5_short_game.description: The sampled rules cover postponed and delayed games but not a game ended before five innings (rain-shortened) nor a suspended game, so settlement in those cases is unknown.
first5_markets#f5_short_game.what_would_resolve: Obtain full rule documents and a settled example of a shortened game.

first5_markets#f5_starter_change_settlem.description: The sampled F5 text has no pitcher clause, so starter-change non-voiding is an inference from silence; also unstated is the F5 settlement when a game is called during the fifth, including whether the home team's unplayed bottom of the fifth counts, and how the Tie strike correlates with the spread and total strikes in that case.
first5_markets#f5_starter_change_settlem.what_would_resolve: Full Kalshi rule documents for KXMLBF5 and a settled example of a starter scratch and of a game called in the fifth.

first5_markets#f5_trip_penalty_variation.description: How much of the second-look penalty is pitcher-specific (arsenal width) versus league-wide, and whether it changed with rules (pitch clock, defensive shifts) is not established.
first5_markets#f5_trip_penalty_variation.what_would_resolve: Estimate trip-specific run rates by arsenal cluster on 2021+ data.

first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_clos.description: Closer and setup assignments are team conventions, not published; close-and-late usage is inferred from game logs, and bullpen availability announcements are partial.
first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_clos.what_would_resolve: Build bullpen-role classification from leverage-index usage and add beat-report capture.

first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_f7_f.description: The 9th-inning markets resolve to a Fair Price if the game is called before the inning completes, but only the 9th-inning strike was sampled; whether other innings of KXMLBINNINGTOTAL and KXMLBINNINGWIN use the same clause, and how a suspended game resumed later is treated, is unseen (the F3/F7 series moved to first5_markets).
first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_f7_f.what_would_resolve: Retrieve full rules and a settled shortened-game example for F3/F5/F7.

first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_inni.description: Only the 9th-inning strike of KXMLBINNINGTOTAL and KXMLBINNINGWIN was sampled; whether innings 2-8 or extra innings exist as strikes, and how a skipped or unplayed inning, an extra-innings inning with the automatic runner, or a shortened game settles, is unknown, so mlb.inning_index_scoring_profile may cover contracts that do not exist.
first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_inni.what_would_resolve: List of live INNINGTOTAL/INNINGWIN event tickers across a season with their inning indices and rule text.

first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_misf.description: After the reconciliation only KXMLBRFI, KXMLBINNINGTOTAL and KXMLBINNINGWIN remain; the inputs mlb.f3_split and mlb.tto and the PA dataset still carry F3/F5-oriented content inherited from the earlier filing, and whether other inning strikes (innings 2-8) trade at all is unknown.
first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_misf.what_would_resolve: List the live KXMLBINNINGTOTAL/INNINGWIN strikes by inning and drop F-series inputs that serve no inning market.

first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_rfi_.description: KXMLBRFI's sampled rule is one sentence with no postponement, suspension or called-game clause, so settlement of a first-inning market when the game is postponed or suspended in the first inning is unstated.
first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_rfi_.what_would_resolve: Full KXMLBRFI rule document and a settled example of a postponed or rain-shortened first-inning market.

first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_spli.description: Whether any first-inning-specific pitcher skill (warm-up, first-pitch strike) exists beyond what the first-trip PA outcomes show is untested; the chain may already capture it.
first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_spli.what_would_resolve: Estimate variance decomposition of starter first-inning run prevention beyond PA-level skill on multiple seasons.

game_moneyline#ml_gamewinner_rules.description: KXMLBGAME and KXMLBSTGAME rules are both sampled (postponement within two days stays open; cancellation or a longer delay settles at a fair price), but neither says how a suspended game resumed on a later date or a rain-shortened official game settles.
game_moneyline#ml_gamewinner_rules.what_would_resolve: Kalshi treatment of suspended and rain-shortened games for KXMLBGAME and KXMLBSTGAME, or settled examples.

game_moneyline#ml_hfa_mechanism.description: How much of home-field advantage is last-at-bat structure versus park and travel effects is not separable with public data, and may have changed after the 2023 schedule and rule changes.
game_moneyline#ml_hfa_mechanism.what_would_resolve: Estimate HFA by inning and by park with 10+ seasons and check regime shifts after 2023.

game_moneyline#ml_lineup_vintage.description: Public feeds give lineups after posting, but timestamps of when each lineup appeared are not reliably archived, so point-in-time backtests of the lineup edge need own capture.
game_moneyline#ml_lineup_vintage.what_would_resolve: Own capture of lineup and probable-pitcher endpoints for a full season.

game_moneyline#ml_misfiled_series.description: All three series now have sampled rules, but the KXMLBGAME and KXMLBSPREAD samples are postseason games and the STGAME sample a spring game; regular-season wording is unseen, and whether one input set serves postseason, regular-season and spring contexts is unverified.
game_moneyline#ml_misfiled_series.what_would_resolve: Sample regular-season KXMLBGAME and KXMLBSPREAD rules and compare clauses with the postseason samples.

game_moneyline#ml_spring_tie.description: KXMLBSTGAME pays only 'If Cleveland wins' and has no tie clause, while spring-training games can end tied; whether a tie resolves both team markets No, voids at a fair price, or cannot occur under the rules of the sampled game is not stated.
game_moneyline#ml_spring_tie.what_would_resolve: Full KXMLBSTGAME rule document or a settled example of a tied spring game.

game_total_and_team_total#tot_extras_sco.description: The sampled rules for game and team totals do not state whether extra-inning runs count nor how postponed, suspended or shortened games settle; the catalog assumes extras count without evidence.
game_total_and_team_total#tot_extras_sco.what_would_resolve: Retrieve the full rules for KXMLBTOTAL and KXMLBTEAMTOTAL and an extra-inning settled example.

game_total_and_team_total#tot_park_axis_.description: wind_vector_park needs each park's field orientation (home-plate-to-center-field bearing) and wall geometry; no source for these fields is named in required_data, and forecast APIs supply wind direction only in compass terms.
game_total_and_team_total#tot_park_axis_.what_would_resolve: A verified table of park orientations (e.g. derived from stadium coordinates or published park diagrams) joined to the forecast archive.

game_total_and_team_total#tot_postseason.description: MLB's automatic extra-innings runner rule (permanent since 2023) applies to regular-season games only, and the sampled totals are postseason games, so extras_run_contribution must use the bases-empty regime for them; what remains open is whether the contract counts extra-inning runs at all (the text is silent) and confirmation that no 2026 rule change extended the runner to the postseason.
game_total_and_team_total#tot_postseason.what_would_resolve: Read the 2026 Official Baseball Rules extra-innings provision and obtain Kalshi wording on whether extras count toward totals.

game_total_and_team_total#tot_series_dep.description: Whether game totals within one postseason series are dependent beyond the listed starters (bullpen fatigue carried across consecutive days, repeated matchups, weather fronts) is not established; the series-length markets that motivated this item moved to the playoff-series archetype.
game_total_and_team_total#tot_series_dep.what_would_resolve: Compare residuals of game totals for consecutive games of the same series against a model with independent games.

game_total_and_team_total#tot_strike_wor.description: KXMLBTEAMTOTAL title says 'over 7.5' while the rule says '8+', and the KXMLBTOTAL rule text reads 'collectively score more 8.5 runs' with the word 'than' missing; both read as the same event (9+ runs and 8+ runs respectively), so this is most likely a typographical omission, not an integer-versus-half-run convention; low priority.
game_total_and_team_total#tot_strike_wor.what_would_resolve: Confirm floor_strike construction from market metadata for several rungs.

game_total_and_team_total#tot_weather_re.description: Whether free forecast sources resolve stadium-level wind direction and speed well enough to extract the park-relative component is unverified.
game_total_and_team_total#tot_weather_re.what_would_resolve: Compare free forecast winds with stadium sensor data or Statcast flight residuals.

hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_bvp_sam.description: Batter-versus-pitcher and pitch-type-specific splits are too sparse for most pairs; whether a shrunk batter_vs_pitch term beats platoon-only is not established and risks adding noise.
hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_bvp_sam.what_would_resolve: Run a held-out comparison of platoon-only versus shrunk pitch-type matchup on logged PA outcomes.

hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_hrr_cha.description: KXMLBHRR (hits plus runs plus RBIs) is live here but only slot-level rbi_opportunity and run_scoring_opportunity exist; the lineup-neighbour on-base chain defined for the RBI archetype (pa_base_out_state_chain) is not available to this record, so the runs and RBI components are modelled more crudely than in the RBI archetype.
hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_hrr_cha.what_would_resolve: Share one base-out chain input between the hits and RBI archetypes once the catalog merge defines it, then compare HRR rung calibration with and without it.

hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_lineup_.description: Markets list before lineups post and the rules settle non-starters at the fair market price, so a point-in-time hitter model needs the confirmed-lineup timestamp, but public feeds do not archive when each card appeared; historical backtests of the start gate need own capture.
hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_lineup_.what_would_resolve: Own capture of the schedule/gamefeed lineup endpoint with timestamps for a full season.

hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_misfile.description: After the reconciliation hits allowed (KXMLBHA) moved to pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks and the All-Star hits and Derby longest-HR series to all_star_week_events; the three remaining series (hits, total bases, hits+runs+RBIs) were each sampled for one postseason game, so regular-season wording is unseen.
hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_misfile.what_would_resolve: Sample regular-season KXMLBHIT, KXMLBTB and KXMLBHRR rules and compare participation clauses.

hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_regime_.description: Post-2023 rule changes (shift ban, bigger bases) altered BABIP and extra-base mix, and the outcome model's stability across rule regimes is unproven for 2026.
hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_regime_.what_would_resolve: Check calibration of the outcome model by season and refit with regime indicators.

hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_settlem.description: The sampled rules do not name the data source nor the treatment of postponed, suspended or shortened games; later scoring changes (hit/error) could alter total bases or hits after settlement.
hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_settlem.what_would_resolve: Obtain full rule documents and compare settlement values to box scores at game end and 24 hours later.

hitter_home_runs#hr_ball_regime.description: Ball carry changes (ball manufacturing, humidors) shift league HR rate year to year; there is no public per-game measurement of ball properties, so carry regime must be inferred from league HR/FB residuals.
hitter_home_runs#hr_ball_regime.what_would_resolve: Track league-wide HR/FB residual by month and check against a regime-switching term.

hitter_home_runs#hr_derby_rules.description: The only sampled KXMLBHR text is an October 2026 postseason contract; whether regular-season KXMLBHR markets use the same participation gate wording (start plus one plate appearance, fair market price otherwise) is unseen, and Derby and All-Star home-run series now sit in the all-star-week archetype.
hitter_home_runs#hr_derby_rules.what_would_resolve: Sample KXMLBHR rules for a regular-season game and compare the participation clauses.

hitter_home_runs#hr_extras_postponement.description: KXMLBHR text counts home runs 'in' the game originally scheduled for a date but does not say whether extra-inning home runs count, how a postponed or suspended game settles, or what happens in a rain-shortened official game where the hitter loses PAs.
hitter_home_runs#hr_extras_postponement.what_would_resolve: Full KXMLBHR rule document and settled examples of an extra-inning home run and a postponed game.

hitter_home_runs#hr_opp_starter_change.description: The single-game HR ladder is conditional only on the hitter, so a scratch of the opposing starter does not trigger the fair-price branch, yet the only availability input is lineup_pit; the probable-pitcher change risk input defined in first5_markets is not available here and pitcher_hr_vulnerability is evaluated for the announced starter only.
hitter_home_runs#hr_opp_starter_change.what_would_resolve: Define a shared probable-pitcher-change input and evaluate pitcher_hr_vulnerability as a mixture over the announced and replacement starters.

hitter_home_runs#hr_wind_source.description: Stadium-level wind speed and direction at ball height are not exposed by free forecast APIs, which give airport or grid values; whether the resolution is good enough to capture park-specific wind swirl is unverified.
hitter_home_runs#hr_wind_source.what_would_resolve: Compare free forecast winds against paid stadium sensors or Statcast ball-flight residuals.

hitter_rbis_runs_sb#rbi_opportunity_vint.description: Whether the state-level opponent baserunner allowance and lineup vintage can be archived point-in-time for backtests is unverified; lineup cards are public but not versioned.
hitter_rbis_runs_sb#rbi_opportunity_vint.what_would_resolve: Own snapshot capture of lineup cards and starting pitchers.

hitter_rbis_runs_sb#rbi_runs_scope.description: The archetype description includes runs scored, but no runs-scored series exists; only KXMLBRBI and KXMLBSB (one rung each, postseason games) were sampled, so other rungs, regular-season wording and postponement handling are unseen.
hitter_rbis_runs_sb#rbi_runs_scope.what_would_resolve: Re-file KXMLBSB here or review it with the counting-specials record; check whether a runs-scored ladder exists.

hitter_rbis_runs_sb#rbi_sb_battery_timin.description: Savant publishes season-level catcher pop time, runner sprint speed and running-game leaderboards, but a pitcher time-to-plate field and per-play pop time are not confirmed as public; the sb_context input and its combined-time nonlinearity depend on them, and proxies (pitcher SB allowed per opportunity, pickoff and lead data, season pop time) would change the required data.
hitter_rbis_runs_sb#rbi_sb_battery_timin.what_would_resolve: Inspect the Savant leaderboards/CSV exports for time-to-plate and per-play pop time, or confirm a proxy and re-estimate the SB attempt model with it.

hitter_rbis_runs_sb#rbi_sb_green_light.description: Manager 'green light' policy is unobserved and shifts with game state; how stable team steal attempt rates per opportunity are within season is not established.
hitter_rbis_runs_sb#rbi_sb_green_light.what_would_resolve: Estimate split-half persistence of team attempt-per-opportunity and test for managerial change effects.

offfield_markets#off_eoty_electorate.description: Retained because an independent finding was deferred here: KXMLBEOTY left this archetype for season_leaders_and_awards, where the unverified electorate of the executive award is tracked as lea_eoty_electorate; nothing in the Field of Dreams market depends on it.
offfield_markets#off_eoty_electorate.what_would_resolve: Resolve under lea_eoty_electorate by confirming the electorate and ballot of the award named in KXMLBEOTY.

offfield_markets#off_no_deadline.description: KXMLBFODTEAMS resolves all No 'If no Pro Baseball 2027 Field of Dreams Game is announced to have participants or occurs' but states no deadline for the announcement, so a labour-delayed schedule release after the market close has no defined treatment.
offfield_markets#off_no_deadline.what_would_resolve: Kalshi clarification of the announcement deadline or the market close rule for this series.

offfield_markets#off_reselection.description: The market 'resolves immediately on team selection'; the text does not say what happens if an announced club is replaced (as in the 2020 re-plan) or the game is cancelled after selection, nor whether a relocated game still counts as the Field of Dreams Game.
offfield_markets#off_reselection.what_would_resolve: Full rule document or a settled example where participants changed after announcement.

offfield_markets#off_small_n.description: Only two Field of Dreams games have been played and fewer than thirty special-event venue games exist, so staging and selection coefficients rest on very few events and borrowing from other special events may not match this venue's regional logic.
offfield_markets#off_small_n.what_would_resolve: Compile all special-event venue games and test whether distance and marketability effects are homogeneous across events.

offfield_markets#off_unstaged_inputs.description: New inputs defined for series that left this archetype (sale stage hazard, manager award score, esports rating, manager candidate signal) remain defined in this record for catalog consistency but are not staged; integration will still attach them to this archetype unless removed.
offfield_markets#off_unstaged_inputs.what_would_resolve: Detach those inputs from offfield_markets at integration or move them to the archetypes that now hold their series.

offfield_markets#off_venue_status.description: The status of the Dyersville site for 2027 (ownership development plans, field availability, temporary stadium) is known only from press reporting; no official dated record of venue readiness is available to backtest the staging input point-in-time.
offfield_markets#off_venue_status.what_would_resolve: Dated league or site-owner statements on 2027 availability, captured with timestamps.

pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks#erhw_hits.description: KXMLBHA now has sampled rules (same one-batter-faced gate and fair-market-price branch as ER and walks), but the text says only 'hits allowed recorded' and is silent on later scorer changes from error to hit (or back), which move hits-allowed rungs more than any other stat in this archetype.
pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks#erhw_hits.what_would_resolve: Obtain Kalshi's settlement-timing policy for official scoring changes and compare historical scorer-change frequency for hits.

pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks#erhw_join.description: The strength and form of dependence among the H, BB and ER ladders for a start (shared command latent versus mechanical coupling through batters faced) is not established; a Gaussian copula may be inadequate when blow-ups truncate the outing.
pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks#erhw_join.what_would_resolve: Fit candidate joint models on start-level data and compare combined-ladder calibration.

pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks#erhw_scor.description: Whether the official scorer identity and post-game scoring changes are exposed in a public feed with timestamps is unverified, and whether Kalshi settles on the first or the final scored value for hits and earned runs is not stated.
pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks#erhw_scor.what_would_resolve: Capture box score at game end and 24 hours later for a season and compare with settled values.

pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks#erhw_seri.description: Each ladder was sampled for one postseason start and one rung only (4+ ER, 3+ BB, 6+ H); whether other rungs, regular-season variants or different gate wording exist is unseen, and none of the texts addresses postponement or a suspended start.
pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks#erhw_seri.what_would_resolve: Sample several rungs and regular-season KXMLBERA, KXMLBWA and KXMLBHA markets including a postponed game.

pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks#erhw_zero.description: The sampled earned-runs, walks and hits-allowed rules settle once the starter has at least one batter faced and settle scratches or non-starters at the undefined fair market price, but do not say how a starter who throws pitches and leaves before facing a batter settles; sibling records disagree on whether this is a fair-price or a tiny-count settlement.
pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks#erhw_zero.what_would_resolve: Full rule text or a settled example of a starter removed before facing a batter.

pitcher_outs#outs_cap_disclosure.description: Announced pitch caps and innings limits are disclosed by teams in press conferences and beat reports, not in a structured feed, so the strongest ceiling input has no clean point-in-time public source.
pitcher_outs#outs_cap_disclosure.what_would_resolve: Build a news-extraction capture of manager pre-game statements and beat writers, or acquire a licensed feed that tags rehab starts and caps.

pitcher_outs#outs_constants.description: Pitches per PA above about 4.2, caps of 85-110 pitches, out probability of 0.68-0.78, delay probability and the claim that managers nearly never pull at outs 19-20 are stated without cited basis; the level of exit-lattice mass at inning boundaries is unestablished even if its persistence is addressed.
pitcher_outs#outs_constants.what_would_resolve: Estimate each from 2021-2025 start logs and PA events and replace the author's constants with fitted values and intervals.

pitcher_outs#outs_contract_scope.description: Only one KXMLBOUTS market (the 15+ rung for one postseason start) was sampled; whether other rungs exist, how a postponed or suspended start settles, and whether outs recorded after a long delay but in the same start count are not stated in the text.
pitcher_outs#outs_contract_scope.what_would_resolve: Sample KXMLBOUTS rules for several rungs and regular-season dates, including a postponed or suspended game.

pitcher_outs#outs_exit_lattice_stability.description: Whether manager-specific exit lattices persist across seasons (and across new managers or new bullpen constructions) is untested; the lattice may be mostly league-wide convention, which would make the manager shrinkage constant too small.
pitcher_outs#outs_exit_lattice_stability.what_would_resolve: Estimate manager lattice persistence by split-half across seasons and compare cross-validated rung log loss.

pitcher_outs#outs_hazard_naming.description: The starter exit-hazard object appears under three ids across sibling archetypes (leash/sp_workload, sp_hook_hazard_curve, exit_boundary_mass); duplicates in the catalog would be fitted separately and drift apart.
pitcher_outs#outs_hazard_naming.what_would_resolve: Define one shared hazard-model input and map the strikeout, outs and earned-run records to it.

pitcher_outs#outs_lineup_vintage.description: The lineup-dependent outs profile needs the confirmed card but public feeds do not archive card post times, and the pre-card state must be a mixture over the team's usual orders.
pitcher_outs#outs_lineup_vintage.what_would_resolve: Own capture of lineup posts with timestamps for a season.

pitcher_strikeouts#ks_abs_challenge_data.description: mlb.abs_challenge_regime needs 2026 pitch-level challenge events (who challenged, original call, overturn, challenges remaining) and edge-pitch called-strike rates; no public export of these fields has been confirmed, and 2026 is the only season of the regime, so the shrink factor applied to pre-2026 umpire and framing effects rests on one partial season.
pitcher_strikeouts#ks_abs_challenge_data.what_would_resolve: Confirm a Savant or Stats API field for ABS challenge events and pull a full 2026 season of challenge outcomes by battery.

pitcher_strikeouts#ks_fair_price_definit.description: The rules say a scratched or non-starting pitcher resolves 'to the fair market price' but define neither the price nor when it is struck; a scratch is therefore a priced settlement value that changes P&L for every holder, not a refund at entry, and scratch risk cannot be treated as outside the modelled payoff.
pitcher_strikeouts#ks_fair_price_definit.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's definition of the fair-market-price settlement (reference time and method) and settled examples of scratched starters.

pitcher_strikeouts#ks_latent_state_size.description: Magnitude of the within-start latent 'stuff day' correlation is assumed to be positive but its size by arsenal type is not established from public evidence; if near zero the dispersion input is wasted effort.
pitcher_strikeouts#ks_latent_state_size.what_would_resolve: Estimate rho from pitch-level data on held-out seasons and compare ladder calibration with and without it.

pitcher_strikeouts#ks_lineup_vintage.description: Public MLB feeds expose posted lineups and umpire assignments but historical timestamps of when each appeared are not reliably archived, which makes point-in-time backtests of the lineup-confirmation edge impossible without own capture.
pitcher_strikeouts#ks_lineup_vintage.what_would_resolve: Run own snapshot capture of statsapi schedule/lineup endpoints for a season, or buy a licensed historical feed with timestamps.

pitcher_strikeouts#ks_postponement_rule.description: The sampled KXMLBKS rules say nothing about postponement, suspension, rain-shortened games or a start interrupted by a long delay; whether the market stays open, voids or settles on the partial count is not stated and cannot be inferred from the text.
pitcher_strikeouts#ks_postponement_rule.what_would_resolve: Fetch the full rules PDF/terms for the series and a settled sample of a rain-shortened or postponed game to see actual treatment.

pitcher_strikeouts#ks_shape_constants.description: The step shape of the time-through-the-order penalty, the 0.15-0.40 magnitudes and the 1 mph velocity threshold are stated without a cited basis; TTO penalties are commonly estimated as per-batter familiarity gradients and the audit itself says pitcher-specific decay is more informative.
pitcher_strikeouts#ks_shape_constants.what_would_resolve: Estimate per-batter-index K-rate and velocity-change effects from 2021-2025 play-by-play and compare step versus smooth fits.

pitcher_strikeouts#ks_source_of_truth.description: No data source is named in the sampled rules; later official scoring changes (dropped third strike, scorer changes) could alter a count after settlement and it is unknown whether Kalshi re-reads.
pitcher_strikeouts#ks_source_of_truth.what_would_resolve: Obtain the series' source agency wording and compare settlement values with box scores on edge cases.

pitcher_strikeouts#ks_talent_prior_gap.description: Pitcher-side talent rests on k_rates, pitch_type_whiff and a 120-BF half-life with no stuff-model or projection-system K% prior for arsenal changes, injury returns or rookies, exactly where pitch-level whiff samples are thinnest.
pitcher_strikeouts#ks_talent_prior_gap.what_would_resolve: Add a stuff-quality or projection K% prior (e.g. ZiPS/Steamer or a pitch-model grade) and test it on pitchers with changed arsenals.

pitcher_strikeouts#ks_zero_batter_starte.description: The sampled text settles on strikeouts once the pitcher is a starter with at least one batter faced and settles scratches or non-starters at the undefined fair market price, but does not say how a starter who throws pitches and leaves before facing a batter (injury, ejection, rain) settles.
pitcher_strikeouts#ks_zero_batter_starte.what_would_resolve: Full rule text or a settled example of a starter removed before facing a batter.

player_participation#pp_cba_lockout.description: Any 2027 KXMLBSTART, KXMLBSTARTER or KXMLBPITCH window depends on the CBA that expires Dec 1 2026; a lockout that cancels games would void or shrink the window (treatment unseen), and the labour input is defined in transactions (mlb.labor_stoppage_regime) and not staged here.
player_participation#pp_cba_lockout.what_would_resolve: Stage mlb.labor_stoppage_regime for 2027 windows and obtain the contract treatment of cancelled games.

player_participation#pp_mixed_family.description: KXMLBSTARTER and KXMLBSTARTINGLINEUP are title-only, so whether the starting-pitcher market settles on the announced probable or the actual first pitcher, and whether STARTINGLINEUP differs from KXMLBSTART, is unknown.
player_participation#pp_mixed_family.what_would_resolve: Sample KXMLBSTARTER and KXMLBSTARTINGLINEUP rules text.

player_participation#pp_opp_starter_vint.description: Platoon-driven start decisions depend on the opposing probable starter's identity and hand and when it was announced, but no input carries them; platoon (a duplicate in other archetypes) only stands in for the hand.
player_participation#pp_opp_starter_vint.what_would_resolve: Define an opposing-probable-starter input with announcement timestamp and use it in the manager-decision stage.

player_participation#pp_posting_vintage.description: Historical posting times of lineups and scratch events are not archived by free feeds, so P(late scratch) cannot be calibrated without own capture.
player_participation#pp_posting_vintage.what_would_resolve: Own capture for a full season or licensed feed with timestamps.

player_participation#pp_postseason_regim.description: Both single-game start samples are Oct 14 2026 playoff games, but the rest-day and clinch-rest constructs are regular-season ones; in October stars rarely sit, rosters are round-specific and off days change pitching plans, so the manager-decision stage may not transfer.
player_participation#pp_postseason_regim.what_would_resolve: Fit start probabilities separately for postseason games or add a round/roster-eligibility input and test it.

player_participation#pp_rehab_data.description: Rehab stage information (bullpen sessions, throwing progression) comes from beat reports and team statements, not a structured source; stage timelines per injury class have small samples. Whether the MLB Stats API marks rehab assignments distinctly is also unverified.
player_participation#pp_rehab_data.what_would_resolve: Build a news-extraction dataset of rehab stage reports and outcomes for several seasons.

player_participation#pp_return_scope.description: KXMLBRETURN requires entering a game 'for the Tigers' inside the window but does not say whether postseason games count, how a trade to another club before the return settles, or whether a suspended game resumed inside the window counts.
player_participation#pp_return_scope.what_would_resolve: Full KXMLBRETURN rule document or settled examples of a traded or postseason return.

player_participation#pp_start_rules_trun.description: The sampled KXMLBSTART rules_secondary is cut off at 'An actual plate appearance is ', so a clause that may change settlement (whether a plate appearance is required, how postponement or suspension of the 'originally scheduled' game is handled) is unseen.
player_participation#pp_start_rules_trun.what_would_resolve: Full untruncated KXMLBSTART rule text and a settled example of a postponed game.

player_participation#pp_twoway_plan.description: Whether a two-way player will pitch in a given window depends on a team plan rarely disclosed and unrelated to health alone; the rate of plan changes is not established.
player_participation#pp_twoway_plan.what_would_resolve: Collect historical examples of two-way plan statements and subsequent usage.

season_futures#sf_2027_cancellation.description: KXMLB lists a 2027 championship future while the CBA expires on Dec 1 2026; the sampled text does not say how the market settles if the 2027 season is shortened or the postseason cancelled (as in 1994), and the lockout-scenario input rests on three historical stoppages.
season_futures#sf_2027_cancellation.what_would_resolve: Kalshi wording on cancelled or shortened seasons for championship futures, plus a dated record of 2026-27 negotiation milestones.

season_futures#sf_extremes_short_season.description: Best and worst record use winning percentage and split ties $1/N, but the 100-loss and streak texts do not say how a shortened season, a cancelled game or a suspended game inside a streak is handled; 100 losses is unreachable in a materially shortened season.
season_futures#sf_extremes_short_season.what_would_resolve: Kalshi wording on shortened seasons and suspended games for the 100-loss and streak markets.

season_futures#sf_injury_hazard.description: Reliable timelines for injuries (return dates) are not published in structured form and team disclosure varies, so ROS WAR at risk is estimated with large uncertainty.
season_futures#sf_injury_hazard.what_would_resolve: Use IL transaction dates with injury-type survival curves and add news capture.

season_futures#sf_mixed_families.description: The 55 series include win ladders, divisions, pennants, qualifiers, seeds, division and league unions, exact World Series outcomes, matchups, season extremes, a World Baseball Classic market and a 2027 championship future; only KXMLBWS lacks rules, no sampled text covers a cancelled or shortened season, and the streak texts are silent on postponed or suspended games inside a streak.
season_futures#sf_mixed_families.what_would_resolve: Sample KXMLBWS rules and the streak treatment of postponed or suspended games.

season_futures#sf_playoff_adjustment.description: How much of the October advantage of top rotations and bullpens is real versus noise is hard to estimate from few series per year, so the playoff rating weights are weakly identified.
season_futures#sf_playoff_adjustment.what_would_resolve: Estimate weights on a longer history of playoff series with pooled analysis.

season_futures#sf_projection_vintage.description: Historical preseason projection vintages (ZiPS, Steamer, PECOTA) are not archived reliably for free, which limits calibration of the prior weight k.
season_futures#sf_projection_vintage.what_would_resolve: Collect projections each preseason through own capture or buy the archives.

season_futures#sf_tiebreaker_source.description: The seed tiebreaker order (head-to-head, intradivision, intraleague, last-half record) is an author paraphrase with no cited source, and whether the 12-team bracket is fixed without reseeding (needed for KXMLBMATCHUP) is not stated in any sampled text; the qualifier and seed texts are silent on cancellation.
season_futures#sf_tiebreaker_source.what_would_resolve: MLB's official tiebreaker and postseason-format documentation and the KXMLBWS rules.

season_futures#sf_wbc_rules.description: KXMLBWORLD's sampled text is one sentence: it does not address tournament cancellation, a final shortened by weather or the mercy rule, and the tournament's pitch limits and tiebreakers are stated from memory rather than an official 2026 rulebook.
season_futures#sf_wbc_rules.what_would_resolve: Full KXMLBWORLD rule document and the official World Baseball Classic tournament regulations.

season_leaders_and_awards#lea_cowinner_p.description: AL Comeback Player lists a 'Tie/Co-Winners' outcome, which suggests individual player markets resolve No when the award is shared, but no award text says so; for awards without that outcome the payout to a co-winner (Yes, $1/N or No) is unstated.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_cowinner_p.what_would_resolve: Kalshi clarification of co-winner settlement for each award series or a settled shared-award example.

season_leaders_and_awards#lea_electorate.description: The electorate per award is not sourced: Reliever of the Year voting by retired relievers, and the Hank Aaron, Comeback Player and Executive of the Year electorates, are stated from memory, so the claim that one Plackett-Luce model serves all awards with shared coefficients is unsupported.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_electorate.what_would_resolve: Each awarding body's published voting procedure and historical ballots by award.

season_leaders_and_awards#lea_eoty_elect.description: KXMLBEOTY (moved here from offfield_markets) names only 'the Governing League'; the electorate of the executive award (club executives versus writers or a media outlet) is unverified, so whether the BBWAA-style rank model, public ballots and the manager-centric wins-over-expectation input apply is unknown (carried from off_eoty_electorate).
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_eoty_elect.what_would_resolve: Identify the award Kalshi settles on and its electorate and ballot format.

season_leaders_and_awards#lea_narrative_.description: Narrative (milestones, comeback, positional context) has no agreed quantitative measure and is hard to tag consistently; its effect size beyond WAR and team success may be small.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_narrative_.what_would_resolve: Define narrative flags (milestone, comeback, first-year, position) and test their incremental effect on vote share.

season_leaders_and_awards#lea_qualificat.description: The Triple Crown text (now sampled) says only 'leads their league in batting average', so the qualification standard (3.1 PA per team game and the batter shortfall provision) and tie treatment are not stated in the contract; the sampled playoff-leader text uses counting stats with proportional ties and no qualification, so rate-stat playoff leaders, if they exist, are undefined.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_qualificat.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's rule text for leader markets and the current MLB official-scoring qualification wording.

season_leaders_and_awards#lea_roy_rule.description: The current rookie-eligibility thresholds and any CBA or award-rule changes for 2026 are not verified from an official source here.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_roy_rule.what_would_resolve: Check BBWAA/MLB rules for rookie status and Pipeline eligibility notes.

season_leaders_and_awards#lea_silent_cla.description: All thirty-one series now have sampled rules, but most award texts (MVP, Cy Young, Rookie, Reliever, Manager, Executive, Hank Aaron, Gold Glove, Silver Slugger) have no co-winner or tie clause; the 'Source Agencies' in the finalist rule are not named; the Triple Crown text does not say whether a tie for a category lead counts; and KXMLBTEAMSTAT variants other than most strikeouts thrown are unseen.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_silent_cla.what_would_resolve: Full rule documents for each award series, the list of Source Agencies and settled examples of a shared award.

season_leaders_and_awards#lea_voter_data.description: Individual ballots for BBWAA awards are public only after announcement, and Gold Glove/Silver Slugger voting details (manager ballots, SDI weight) are limited, so voter models for those awards are weakly identified.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_voter_data.what_would_resolve: Collect public ballots across years and verify SDI weighting for Gold Glove.

transactions#tr_filing.description: KXMLBCOACH is title-only, so whether the next-manager market counts interim managers, and its resolution date, is unknown; the NEXTTEAM text is truncated after the extension clause.
transactions#tr_filing.what_would_resolve: Sample KXMLBCOACH rules and the full KXMLBNEXTTEAM text.

transactions#tr_lockout_forecast.description: The labour_stoppage_regime input depends on forecasting a lockout beginning after Dec 1 2026 and its length from three historical stoppages and negotiation reports; the probability and duration are highly uncertain and no public data series codes negotiation state.
transactions#tr_lockout_forecast.what_would_resolve: A coded negotiation timeline from own capture and an out-of-sample check on the 2021-22 episode.

transactions#tr_report_data.description: Whether a historical archive of timestamped reports with outcomes can be assembled from public sources (rather than social platforms with restricted access) is unverified.
transactions#tr_report_data.what_would_resolve: Test a scrape of MLB Trade Rumors and beat-writer feeds for coverage and timestamps.

transactions#tr_settlement_assumed.description: KXMLBTRADE now states its settlement (official MLB processing before the date; later rescission or failed physical still Yes), but the KXMLBNEXTTEAM text says only 'signs a contract with any team' and is truncated, the KXMLBDEBUT text says only 'plays for any MLB team', and neither mentions official announcement, physicals or voiding; KXMLBCOACH is title-only.
transactions#tr_settlement_assumed.what_would_resolve: Full Kalshi rule text for NEXTTEAM, DEBUT and COACH and settled examples of a reported-but-unofficial signing.

transactions#tr_small_n.description: Manager changes and specific transaction types are rare events per year, so hazard estimates have wide uncertainty and cross-sport borrowing may not apply.
transactions#tr_small_n.what_would_resolve: Pool across seasons and cross-league and quantify uncertainty explicitly.

transactions#tr_trade_processing_time.description: KXMLBTRADE requires the trade to be 'officially processed and approved by MLB before' the date but does not say which timestamp is used (league transaction log time, club announcement) or whether 'before Aug 5' includes deals agreed on Aug 4 and processed overnight; borderline deadline deals hinge on this.
transactions#tr_trade_processing_time.what_would_resolve: Kalshi clarification of the processing timestamp source or a settled example of a deal processed after the deadline hour.

unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_derby_dat.description: Whether swing-level Derby data (swing number, takes, BP pitcher, pitch tracking) is publicly retrievable for 2015-2026 was not verified, and only one swing-capped Derby (2026) exists for calibrating volume.
unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_derby_dat.what_would_resolve: Attempt retrieval of one past Derby from Savant and MLB Stats API and record exposed fields.

unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_derby_ext.description: Derby total HR, 500+ ft count, longest HR and highest exit velocity texts are silent on whether swing-off and last-swing extension homers count, and the Round 2 over/under does not say explicitly that a Round 1 exit is No.
unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_derby_ext.what_would_resolve: Kalshi clarification or 2026 settlement values compared with official round-by-round and swing-off homers.

unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_derby_rul.description: The 2026 swing-capped format (20/15/15 swings, last-swing extension, longest-HR Round 1 tiebreak, three-swing swing-offs) comes from press reports; the official rulebook (whether takes count, semifinal pairing rule, pitch limits) could not be fetched (mlb.com blocked).
unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_derby_rul.what_would_resolve: Read the official MLB 2026 Derby rules notes and confirm against 2026 swing-level results.

unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_futures_t.description: Level translation factors for Futures Game prospects (Double-A versus Triple-A versus Low-A) are placeholders, and fewer than ten NL vs AL Futures Games exist to check them against outcomes.
unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_futures_t.what_would_resolve: Calibrate translations on minor-to-major transitions and compare Futures Game predictions over 2015-2025 rosters.

unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_mvp_vote_.description: The ASG MVP is chosen by a panel with a fan ballot component, but the panel composition and fan weight for 2026 were not checked against an MLB source, so the star-bias term cannot be calibrated.
unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_mvp_vote_.what_would_resolve: MLB announcement describing the 2026 MVP voting procedure and fan-vote weight.

unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_small_sam.description: Only about a dozen All-Star Games exist under the current regime, so participation and PA models cannot be validated to the precision a regular-season prop can.
unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_small_sam.what_would_resolve: Pool several years and compare manager-level substitution patterns with a held-out year.

unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_total_hr_.description: KXMLBALLSTARHR counts home runs 'all competing players combined hit' in the All-Star Game and, unlike KXMLBASGHIT/KXMLBASGHR, does not exclude swing-off statistics; whether swing-off homers count toward the 7+ total is not stated.
unreg:all_star_week_events#asw_total_hr_.what_would_resolve: Kalshi rules clarification or a settled market from a year in which the game ended in a swing-off.

unreg:amateur_draft_selection#draft_club.description: Club boards and pre-draft bonus agreements are private; public mocks and leaks are an incomplete and noisy proxy, and their historical archive with exact timestamps is incomplete.
unreg:amateur_draft_selection#draft_club.what_would_resolve: Building an own-capture archive of mocks and insider posts with timestamps over several drafts and measuring their accuracy.

unreg:amateur_draft_selection#draft_comp.description: The rules do not say whether inserted round-1 failed-to-sign compensation picks count toward the 'overall pick' number, nor whether 'top 10' includes the 10th pick; either changes which club holds the settling slot. Prospect Promotion Incentive picks are understood to follow round 1 and so not to renumber slots 1-10 (CBA text not verified here).
unreg:amateur_draft_selection#draft_comp.what_would_resolve: Kalshi clarification or a finalized market whose settlement reveals the numbering convention.

unreg:amateur_draft_selection#draft_lott.description: Exact lottery odds by record rank, the eligibility restrictions on repeat winners and revenue-sharing payors, and the rule that lottery-ineligible clubs pick no higher than 10th (which changes who holds slots 7-10, the settling slots) have not been verified against the CBA text here.
unreg:amateur_draft_selection#draft_lott.what_would_resolve: Read the 2022-2026 CBA draft lottery article or MLB's official lottery odds release.

unreg:amateur_draft_selection#draft_no_s.description: rules_secondary is empty: no source of truth and no clause for a postponed, shortened or cancelled draft or for a prospect withdrawing; a lockout after the 1 December 2026 CBA expiry bears only on 2027-draft series; the sampled 2026 markets are finalized and that draft was held in July 2026.
unreg:amateur_draft_selection#draft_no_s.what_would_resolve: Full rules text for a current-year market, including resolution source and postponement handling.

unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.description: The December 1, 2026 expiry date comes from the catalog input description and the market reviewer note and was not verified against the CBA text here.
unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.what_would_resolve: Check the CBA text and official MLB or MLBPA announcements for the expiry date.

unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.description: 'Number of MLB regular season games played is above 600' is read as league games (2,430 scheduled) but team-games (4,860) are not excluded; on a team-game reading the 600 strike corresponds to only about 20 games per team.
unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.what_would_resolve: Kalshi clarification or rules text stating the counting unit for KXMLBSEASONGAMES.

unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.description: The sampled rules do not say whether suspended or shortened contests count as games played, nor which source counts them (tiebreaker Game 163 was abolished from 2022 and matters only if reinstated).
unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full rules text for KXMLBSEASONGAMES, and any clarification from the market operator.

unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.description: The owners' cost-per-week numerator of the leverage ratio rests on Forbes/Sportico revenue estimates and reported media terms, which are third-party estimates rather than disclosures, so the ratio is uncertain in level and possibly in sign.
unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.what_would_resolve: Audited or league-disclosed revenue splits (e.g. from bargaining filings) or a sensitivity range across estimate sources.

unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.description: Only a handful of comparable stoppages exist, and the current dispute's structural demands (such as a payroll cap) may not match prior cases, so the hazard shape cannot be validated.
unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.what_would_resolve: Track the negotiation as it unfolds and score the hazard model on interim milestones; expand the reference class across leagues.

unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.description: Actual bargaining proposals and private sessions are not public; only leaks and statements are visible, so the gap index is partly guesswork.
unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.what_would_resolve: A systematic log of outlets' reports with confirmation timing; no public source for private proposals exists.

unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.description: Neither rules text says whether games staged with replacement players after an impasse declaration count as 'MLB regular season games' or as the 'first game' for the Opening Day contract.
unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.what_would_resolve: Operator clarification on whether settlement follows the official MLB record regardless of who plays.

unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.description: Opening Day settles on whether the first game occurred prior to May 31, 2027 but the sampled text gives no time zone for a game played near midnight on May 30 or 31.
unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.what_would_resolve: Rules text or operator clarification on the time-zone convention.

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_first.description: The rules do not say whether a 107+ reading published in the live feed or on the broadcast counts if it is later corrected or removed, or whether only the final Statcast record counts, which decides whether feed glitches can settle YES.
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_first.what_would_resolve: Kalshi rules_secondary or a settlement note naming the source and whether later corrections apply.

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_kxmlb.description: KXMLBSTAT is a generic season-stat series and only KXMLBSTAT-26P107-AP was sampled, so which other KXMLBSTAT markets exist, and whether they settle on non-velocity stats, is unknown; the archetype applies only to velocity markets.
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_kxmlb.what_would_resolve: List every KXMLBSTAT market ticker and its rules text; route non-velocity markets to a separate archetype.

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_park_.description: Size and stability of Hawk-Eye park-level speed offsets and how often MLB revises release_speed after games have not been verified here.
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_park_.what_would_resolve: Repeated pulls of Statcast data over a season and visiting-pitcher park residual analysis.

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_sourc.description: The rules name no tracking source and do not define rounding: '107.0+' (named) and '107+' (any) may treat a 106.95 reading differently, and stadium or broadcast radar readings could conflict with Statcast.
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_sourc.what_would_resolve: Kalshi rules_secondary or clarification naming Statcast release speed and its precision.

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_tail_.description: 107 mph lies beyond every tracked pitch; any probability is an extrapolation whose value depends almost entirely on the assumed tail endpoint, which cannot be estimated from data.
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_tail_.what_would_resolve: Biomechanical evidence on the physical ceiling of arm speed or a sensitivity analysis over generalised-Pareto shape parameters.

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_tempe.description: The size of the cold-air velocity penalty, which drives the claimed convex lift in the tail, has not been verified against published studies or fitted on Statcast data here.
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_tempe.what_would_resolve: Fit the temperature coefficient on 2021-2025 Statcast fastballs with pitcher random effects and compare with published estimates.

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_windo.description: 'any game during the season (regular season and playoffs)' does not say whether spring training, the All-Star Game or suspended-game completions count, nor whether World Baseball Classic or other non-MLB games pitched by MLB arms (which tracking systems record) count; the 'Pro Baseball season' wording most plausibly excludes them.
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_windo.what_would_resolve: Full rules text or a settlement note listing included game types.

unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.description: Retained for a deferred finding: the generic families it covered left this archetype (KXMLBTEAMSTAT to season_leaders_and_awards, KXMLBSTAT to the velocity archetype, KXMLBLSTREAK to season_futures). For the remaining series only one rung or one player per family was sampled, so other KXMLBSISTREAK, KXMLBNEXTHR and KXMLBPLAYOFFHRS variants are unseen.
unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.what_would_resolve: Sample further strikes and players for the remaining families and compare wording.

unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.description: Five series with three mechanisms remain in one unregistered archetype (postseason league counts, player home-run exposure markets, a pitcher scoreless streak); one input list serves none of them fully, and the streak market has no other natural home.
unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.what_would_resolve: Split the bucket into postseason-count, player-exposure and streak families with their own catalog entries.

unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.description: KXMLBSERIESHR counts a named player's home runs across the series and KXMLBNEXTHR any MLB game in a window, but neither text says how a player who is injured, benched or removed from the roster settles (No on the count versus a fair price), nor whether KXMLBNEXTHR includes postseason games if the window extends into October.
unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.what_would_resolve: Full rule documents for KXMLBSERIESHR and KXMLBNEXTHR or settled examples where the player missed games.

unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.description: KXMLBSISTREAK counts scoreless outs at one third of an inning but does not say whether an unearned run or an inherited runner scoring after the pitcher exits breaks the streak; postseason innings are excluded because the text ends the count when the regular season concludes; the probability differs materially between definitions.
unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.what_would_resolve: Full KXMLBSISTREAK rule document or a settled example where an unearned or inherited run occurred during a streak.

unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.description: The per-inning scoreless probability for an elite starter is estimated from a Markov chain on shrunk rates, but long streaks are selected on luck (low BABIP, strand rate), so the survival input may overstate persistence unless the as-of rates are regressed harder for pitchers already on a streak.
unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.what_would_resolve: Backtest streak continuation probabilities on all 30+ inning streaks since 1990 against the survival model.

unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.description: KXMLBWALKOFFS is titled 'Pro Baseball Walk-Off Home Runs' while its rule counts any walk-off ('The way the run scores does not matter'); if some strikes or later versions count only walk-off home runs, the per-game rate falls to roughly a third, so the wording per market must be read before pricing.
unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.what_would_resolve: Read the rules for every live KXMLBWALKOFFS strike and confirm the counted event.

unreg:playoff_series_markets#ply_game_de.description: Whether game outcomes within a series are independent beyond known starter and fatigue effects (momentum, shared injuries) is not settled and small samples limit tests.
unreg:playoff_series_markets#ply_game_de.what_would_resolve: Fit game-level models with and without series random effects on 1995-2025 postseason games and compare score distributions.

unreg:playoff_series_markets#ply_host_de.description: KXMLBPLAYOFFHOST says only 'hosts at least 8 playoff games'. Whether a designated home game played at a temporary or borrowed park (Athletics in Sacramento 2025-27, Rays at Steinbrenner Field in 2025) or moved to a neutral site counts as hosted is not defined.
unreg:playoff_series_markets#ply_host_de.what_would_resolve: Kalshi clarification or full rules stating whether settlement uses the designated home team or the venue.
